column1: # The rule registry: ONE row per rule. Columns (TAB separated): name, kind, enforcer, waiver, what.
#   name      kebab-case, says what is wrong; does not change when rules are added. A check prints `FAIL <name>: <n> place(s)`.
#   kind      check = a script decides (a failure fails the gate) | hint = a script lists candidates and a person or the Challenger decides | review = no script; read by a reviewer
#   enforcer  the script(s) under scripts/ (comma separated), or `review`
#   waiver    how a place is excused (a marker, a baseline, an option), or `-` when it cannot be
# references/rules.md holds the table generated from this file (scripts/rules_table.py --write); the prose of each rule stays in rules.md.

column4: phase 2 only: PHASE2_ALLOWED_DIFF (a file of approved LO-HI ranges)
column5: The built image equals the reference byte for byte (phase 1 always; phase 2 until the approved removals).
No hex address as a code operand: give the target a label (`#<label` / `#>label` for half an address).

column4: `// NOT-ADDRESS: reason` on the line
column5: No lo/hi pair of immediates that builds the address of a named variable or label.
No Ghidra placeholder name (DAT_, LAB_, SUB_, FUN_ ...) anywhere in the source, comments included.

column5: No `unk` name, TODO(name) / TODO(block) marker or `STATUS:  unknown` banner left at the end of phase 1.
An anonymous label only in one routine, at most two steps and 40 lines from its use, nothing else referring to it.

column5: Comment text wraps at 128 columns; a data row's comment at 100.

column5: No line longer than 150 columns.

column5: A label line's summary is at most 80 characters; the detail is a block comment above the label.

column5: A data-row comment keeps `// [addr]` and does not repeat the row (operand names, an ASCII dump).

column4: tools/comment_baseline.tsv
column5: A `TODO(tag):` marker has a headline sentence after it.

column4: `TODO(phase2): remove? unreferenced, never executed` above the label
column5: A label nothing refers to is dead code or leftover data and carries the removal marker.
The SECTION banners tile the image from first to last byte: no gap, no overlap.

column4: COMMIT_BINARIES in project.config
column5: Game binaries are not committed unless the owner chose to (a recommendation, not a ban).
originals/, dumps/, reference/ and build/ are in .gitignore when the directories exist.
Every file in originals/ matches the SHA-256 recorded when it was gathered.
The routine tests (code run in the 6510 simulator against Python models) pass on the current build.

column4: timing-tolerant set (check-t), --lag N, GOLDEN_PIN
column5: The per-frame state of the scenarios equals the recorded traces (exact, or timing-tolerant after a byte-changing step).
The project's framework/ equals the skill's master; a local edit is moved into the skill or removed.
A self-modified operand is named `label:operand`, with a `// SMC: kind patched by routine` line and a trailing SMC marker.

column4: `// NOT-POINTERS: reason`
column5: Pointer data is `.word label` or `#<label` / `#>label`, never a literal, so a table or block can move.
A table of fixed-size records, or a stream of events, is written one record per row with the terminator on its own row.
A state value ($00 / $80 / $FF), a stride or a count the code repeats gets a constant; the raw value is written once.
A routine that spins on a hardware register, patches its own code, calls ROM, switches banking or relies on the stack pointer carries a TODO(port) line.

column4: `docs/relocation_hazards.md` (documented hazards)
column5: Nothing breaks when the image or a variable moves: indirect addressing, pointer tables, SMC, aligned bases.

column4: `TODO(name)` until the evidence is there
column5: A name that claims a role needs the document AND an observation (the evidence ladder); a document alone is not enough.
What art, a sound or a game mode IS is asked of the owner after the code and a tracer run; never invented.
The original author's word is used, not a synonym, in identifiers, comments and docs alike.
A routine with local labels is a scope, each label named for what it means; a label used elsewhere is global with a proper name.
A variable or table inside the image gets an in-stream label, not a `.label X = $ADDR` line in a symbols file.
Every string is written as readable text through the game's encoding, never as `.byte` rows.

Phase 1: every `[ADDR:bytes MNEMONIC]` reference and the Ghidra XREF comments stay with their lines and labels. Phase 2 keeps the `[ADDR:bytes]` references and drops the XREF lists (no-xref-in-phase2).
An instruction whose operand bytes are another instruction (the BIT-skip trick) is written `.byte $2C` with a comment saying so.
Every table has a column list above its label: what it is, record count and size, who reads it, one line per field.
The block above a routine says what it does and why; In / Out / Clobbers when not obvious; `probably` when unsure.
A layout assumption (page boundary, adjacent tables, a VIC-bank offset) is written as an `.assert` next to it.
A hardware-fixed base is ONE absolute constant, and every anchored block is asserted against it.
A bug of the original is reproduced, recorded in docs/gameplay.md and tagged `TODO(phase2): original bug:`.
Generated pictures live in docs/gfx/, named by content, never in build/, dumps/ or /tmp.

column4: Skip it is a valid answer
column5: A question about graphics shows an in-play screen with numbered regions and one short question each, never a single tile code.
State that holds an address is not behaviour: it stays out of the golden-trace state.
Emulator tests run unattended and are judged by screenshot, not by a PC sample; the emulator never takes the desktop focus.
An original is never attached to an emulator directly: VICE runs scratch copies.

column4: SLICE_REVIEW="off" in project.config, or `slice-merge --skip-review "reason"` (recorded in docs/reviews/)
column5: A slice is reviewed by a second agent (the Challenger) before it merges: a record for the slice's current diff, answering every review rule, with VERDICT: PASS.

column4: `docs/start_contract.md` lists what an inject launch of phase 1 needs and why the game cannot set it itself
column5: The build starts at a point in the game's own code with a plain boot (`LAUNCH_MODE=sys`); phase 1 may use `inject` only as a recorded fallback, and phase 2 never: its start contract is code in the Boot routine.

column4: PHASE2_LABEL_STYLE="standard" in project.config (else listed as a hint), or a tools/comment_baseline.tsv entry
column5: Phase 2 source has no Ghidra XREF lists: they point at phase 1 addresses and go stale (phase 1 keeps them as the trace to the original).

column4: PHASE2_LABEL_STYLE="standard" in project.config (else listed as a hint), or a tools/comment_baseline.tsv entry
column5: Phase 2 zero_page.asm declares its variables in a `virtual` segment (`name: .byte $00`, one per variable), not as `.label NAME = $ADDR` lines.

column4: PHASE2_LABEL_STYLE="standard" in project.config (else listed as a hint), or a tools/comment_baseline.tsv entry
column5: A comment states what a thing is; how it was found (Rung, Observed, frame numbers, a run, a docs/ path) is evidence and lives in docs/.

column4: PHASE2_LABEL_STYLE="standard" in project.config (else listed as a hint), or a tools/comment_baseline.tsv entry
column5: A comment names a routine, not its address, when a label has that address (the symbol file TRACE_SYM / TRACE_SYM_P1 decides); data and hardware addresses in an explanation of a layout stay.
A label-line comment whose words are all in the label's own name (`High byte of x`, `element 5 of x_tbl`) adds nothing: no comment is better.
A variable's comment fits at the end of its line (about 80 characters), running across the two lines of a `_lo` / `_hi` pair when it needs to; a block comment is for a group header or a real hazard.
